$comment: The injection bank (ALE-36, grown from ALE-33's 16 seed cases). Each case is free text a player could type at the game. Three walls stand behind it: the text enters the prompt inside a delimited block labelled as player speech and never as instruction; the engine validates every mutation, so obeying an injection still cannot change the world; and the sandbox bounds anything the model tries to run. Every case is run against all three by services/gm/tests/test_injection.py, with a model that is hostile by construction -- the scripted fake obeys the injection, because the question is not whether the model resists but whether it matters when it does not. The same file drives the `injection-bank` entry in the replay regression bank (docs/regression-bank.md): every `demands` is attempted through the real engine and must come back refused, and the recorded session replays to identical hashes in CI. One copy, both languages, like contracts/gm-tools.json. Add a case whenever a new vector turns up; the tests iterate the file, so a new entry needs no new test -- but run `pnpm --filter @deliberate/server bank:write` afterwards, because the recording is derived from it.

families.instruction-override: Text that tells the game master to stop following its own instructions, usually by claiming authority it does not have.
families.tool-markup: Tool-call syntax typed into dialogue, hoping something parses it. Nothing does: a tool call is a structured block from the model, never text from a player.
families.fake-verdict: The player asserting an engine outcome. Only a GmToolResult writes the verified ledger, so a claimed hit stays a claim.
families.prompt-disclosure: Asking for the system prompt, the tool schemas, or the memory blocks, directly or by indirection.
families.fence-escape: Trying to end the player-speech block early and have the rest read as prompt.
families.sandbox-escape: Code the player wants run in the `python` tool: filesystem, network, credentials, or an endless loop.
families.say-exfiltration: Using an NPC's mouth as the exit: `say` reaches the player exactly like narration does.
families.obfuscation: The same demands, encoded or hidden, so a naive string check would miss them.
families.resource: Text sized or shaped to blow the prompt budget rather than to change behaviour.
